revision.comment: 新しいページ：谷地久保古墳（福島県白河市にある古墳）。
revision.text:
{{日本の古墳 |名称 = 谷地久保古墳 |画像 = [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, gaikan.jpg|280px]]
墳丘 |別名 = |所属 = |所在地 = [[福島県]][[白河市]]本沼岩井戸 |緯度度 = 37|緯度分 = 8|緯度秒 = 22.80 |経度度 =140|経度分 = 17|経度秒 = 1.75 |ISO = JP-07 |形状 = [[円墳]] |規模 = 直径17m
高さ3.7m |埋葬施設 = [[横口式石槨]] |出土品 = |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]後半-[[8世紀]]初頭 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 国の[[史跡]]「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」に包含 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = |地図2 = {{Location map|Japan Fukushima|label=谷地久保
古墳|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.png|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''谷地久保古墳'''（やちくぼこふん）は、[[福島県]][[白河市]]本沼（もとぬま）にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+白河地域の首長墓{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}} !古墳名 !形状 !埋葬施設 !築造時期 |- |[[下総塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||[[横穴式石室]]||[[6世紀]]後半 |- |舟田中道1号墳||[[円墳]]||横穴式石室||[[7世紀]]前半-7世紀中葉 |- |'''谷地久保古墳'''||円墳||[[横口式石槨]]||7世紀後半-[[8世紀]]初頭 |- |[[野地久保古墳]]||[[上円下方墳]]||横口式石槨||7世紀後半-8世紀初頭 |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|[[野地久保古墳]]方向を望む
（左奥の樹叢）}}]] 福島県南部、[[阿武隈川]]左岸の三方を丘陵に囲まれた丘陵南斜面に築造された古墳である。[[野地久保古墳]]と同じ谷の北西400メートルに位置する。[[1926年]]（[[大正]]15年）・[[1983年]]（[[昭和]]58年）に石室実測調査が実施されているほか、[[2001年|2001]]・[[2003年]]（[[平成]]13・15年）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は円形。墳丘は2段築成で、1段目は直径17メートル、2段目は直径10メートル、墳丘裾部からの高さは最大3.7メートルを測る{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。主体部の埋葬施設は[[横口式石槨]]で、南方向に開口する。安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石によって構築され、山寄せの立地と合わせて近畿地方の横口式石槨と共通する特徴を示すとして注目される。盗掘に遭っているため副葬品は詳らかでない{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 この谷地久保古墳は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]後半-[[8世紀]]初頭頃の築造と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。南東の野地久保古墳とともに畿内的な横口式石槨を有する特異な古墳であり、被葬者は古代[[白河郡]]における盟主的な立場の人物と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。また、南方に所在する[[下総塚古墳]]（後期の首長墓）と舟田中道遺跡（後期の豪族居館）とともに古墳時代の[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]として認知され、周辺に展開する[[関和久官衙遺跡]]（推定白河郡衙跡）・[[借宿廃寺跡]]からなる古代の白河官衙遺跡群と合わせて、古代白河郡の中心地を示す遺跡群の一角として重要視される古墳である。 古墳域は[[2015年]]（平成17年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「白河舟田・本沼遺跡群」のうち）。 === 来歴 === * [[1926年]]（[[大正]]15年）、測量調査（岩越二郎、[[1936年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1983年]]（[[昭和]]58年）、測量調査（[[網干善教]]、[[1984年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[2001年|2001]]・[[2003年]]（[[平成]]13・15年）、国の史跡指定に向けた発掘調査：第3・4次調査（白河市教育委員会、[[2002年|2002]]・[[2005年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[2015年]]（平成17年）7月14日、国の[[史跡]]に指定（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|00003447|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}。 == 埋葬施設 == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, sekkaku-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石槨 開口部}}]] 主体部の埋葬施設としては[[横口式石槨]]が構築されており、南方向に開口する。石槨の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * 玄室：長さ1.44メートル、幅1.38メートル、高さ1.19メートル * 玄門：長さ0.425メートル、下端幅0.71メートル、高さ0.84メートル * 羨道：長さ0.815メートル、幅0.97メートル、高さ1.17メートル 石槨の石材は安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石。現在は奥壁・側壁・天井石・床石が遺存する。石槨の前庭部は南にハ字形に開き、壁面には川原石を積み、底面には扁平な川原石を敷設する{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 石槨の特徴としては[[中尾山古墳]]（[[奈良県]][[明日香村]]）との共通性が指摘される。中尾山古墳と同様に火葬壺が置かれたとする説の一方、中尾山古墳よりも一回り大きいことから改葬墓とする説もある{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 File:Yachikubo Kofun, sekkaku-3.jpg|石槨内部 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（白河市設置） * 地方自治体発行 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2011|chapter=|title=国指定史跡 白河舟田・本沼遺跡群 白河官衙遺跡群（白河市文化財パンフレット）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}}} * 事典類 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=鈴木功|year=2002|chapter=谷地久保古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典|続 日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490105991|ref={{Harvid|谷地久保古墳（続古墳）|2002}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=|chapter=[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%99%BD%E6%B2%B3%E8%88%9F%E7%94%B0-%E6%9C%AC%E6%B2%BC%E9%81%BA%E8%B7%A1%E7%BE%A4-1444165 白河舟田-本沼遺跡群]|title=国指定史跡ガイド|publisher=[[講談社]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|白河舟田-本沼遺跡群（国指定史跡）}}}} - リンクは[[朝日新聞社]]「[[コトバンク]]」。 == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite journal|和書|author=岩越二郎|title=西白河郡烏峠付近の遺蹟遺物に就いて（下）|date=1936|publisher=岩磐郷土研究会|journal=岩磐史談|volume=|number=9|pages=|url=|naid=|doi=|ref=}} * {{Cite journal|和書|author=福島雅儀|title=福島県の終末期古墳・二例|date=1983|publisher=福島県文化センター|journal=文化福島|volume=|number=|pages=|url=|naid=|doi=|ref=}} * {{Cite journal|和書|author=[[網干善教]]ほか|title=東北地方南部における終末期古墳の調査|date=1984|publisher=関西大学考古学研究室|journal=考古学研究紀要|volume=|number=4|pages=|url=|naid=|doi=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2002|chapter=|title=谷地久保古墳発掘調査報告書 第3次調査（白河市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第36集）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2005|chapter=|title=谷地久保古墳発掘調査報告書 第4次調査（白河市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第41集）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]] ** [[野地久保古墳]] ** [[下総塚古墳]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Yachikubo Kofun}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|00003447|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} 古墳|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.png|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''谷地久保古墳'''（やちくぼこふん）は、[[福島県]][[白河市]]本沼（もとぬま）にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+白河地域の首長墓{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}} !古墳名 !形状 !埋葬施設 !築造時期 |- |[[下総塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||[[横穴式石室]]||[[6世紀]]後半 |- |舟田中道1号墳||[[円墳]]||横穴式石室||[[7世紀]]前半-7世紀中葉 |- |'''谷地久保古墳'''||円墳||[[横口式石槨]]||7世紀後半-[[8世紀]]初頭 |- |[[野地久保古墳]]||[[上円下方墳]]||横口式石槨||7世紀後半-8世紀初頭 |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|[[野地久保古墳]]方向を望む
（左奥の樹叢）}}]] 福島県南部、[[阿武隈川]]左岸の三方を丘陵に囲まれた丘陵南斜面に築造された古墳である。[[野地久保古墳]]と同じ谷の北西400メートルに位置する。[[1926年]]（[[大正]]15年）・[[1983年]]（[[昭和]]58年）に石室実測調査が実施されているほか、[[2001年|2001]]・[[2003年]]（[[平成]]13・15年）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は円形。墳丘は2段築成で、1段目は直径17メートル、2段目は直径10メートル、墳丘裾部からの高さは最大3.7メートルを測る{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。主体部の埋葬施設は[[横口式石槨]]で、南方向に開口する。安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石によって構築され、山寄せの立地と合わせて近畿地方の横口式石槨と共通する特徴を示すとして注目される。盗掘に遭っているため副葬品は詳らかでない{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 この谷地久保古墳は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]後半-[[8世紀]]初頭頃の築造と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。南東の野地久保古墳とともに畿内的な横口式石槨を有する特異な古墳であり、被葬者は古代[[白河郡]]における盟主的な立場の人物と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。また、南方に所在する[[下総塚古墳]]（後期の首長墓）と舟田中道遺跡（後期の豪族居館）とともに古墳時代の[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]として認知され、周辺に展開する[[関和久官衙遺跡]]（推定白河郡衙跡）・[[借宿廃寺跡]]からなる古代の白河官衙遺跡群と合わせて、古代白河郡の中心地を示す遺跡群の一角として重要視される古墳である。 古墳域は[[2015年]]（平成17年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「白河舟田・本沼遺跡群」のうち）。 === 来歴 === * [[1926年]]（[[大正]]15年）、測量調査（岩越二郎、[[1936年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1983年]]（[[昭和]]58年）、測量調査（[[網干善教]]、[[1984年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1988年]]（昭和63年）、福島県指定史跡に指定。 * [[2001年|2001]]・[[2003年]]（[[平成]]13・15年）、国の史跡指定に向けた発掘調査：第3・4次調査（白河市教育委員会、[[2002年|2002]]・[[2005年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[2015年]]（平成17年）7月14日、国の[[史跡]]に指定（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|00003447|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}。 == 埋葬施設 == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, sekkaku-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石槨 開口部}}]] 主体部の埋葬施設としては[[横口式石槨]]が構築されており、南方向に開口する。石槨の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * 玄室：長さ1.44メートル、幅1.38メートル、高さ1.19メートル * 玄門：長さ0.425メートル、下端幅0.71メートル、高さ0.84メートル * 羨道：長さ0.815メートル、幅0.97メートル、高さ1.17メートル 石槨の石材は安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石。現在は奥壁・側壁・天井石・床石が遺存する。石槨の前庭部は南にハ字形に開き、壁面には川原石を積み、底面には扁平な川原石を敷設する{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 石槨の特徴としては[[中尾山古墳]]（[[奈良県]][[明日香村]]）との共通性が指摘される。中尾山古墳と同様に火葬壺が置かれたとする説の一方、中尾山古墳よりも一回り大きいことから改葬墓とする説もある{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 File:Yachikubo Kofun, sekkaku-3.jpg|石槨内部 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} 高さ3.7m |埋葬施設 = [[横口式石槨]] |出土品 = |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]後半-[[8世紀]]初頭 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 国の[[史跡]]「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」に包含 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = |地図2 = {{Location map|Japan Fukushima|label=谷地久保
古墳|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.png|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''谷地久保古墳'''（やちくぼこふん）は、[[福島県]][[白河市]]本沼（もとぬま）にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+白河地域の首長墓{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}} !古墳名 !形状 !埋葬施設 !築造時期 |- |[[下総塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||[[横穴式石室]]||[[6世紀]]後半 |- |舟田中道1号墳||[[円墳]]||横穴式石室||[[7世紀]]前半-7世紀中葉 |- |'''谷地久保古墳'''||円墳||[[横口式石槨]]||7世紀後半-[[8世紀]]初頭 |- |[[野地久保古墳]]||[[上円下方墳]]||横口式石槨||7世紀後半-8世紀初頭 |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|[[野地久保古墳]]方向を望む
（左奥の樹叢）}}]] 福島県南部、[[阿武隈川]]左岸の三方を丘陵に囲まれた丘陵南斜面に築造された古墳である。[[野地久保古墳]]と同じ谷の北西400メートルに位置する。[[1926年]]（[[大正]]15年）・[[1983年]]（[[昭和]]58年）に石室実測調査が実施されているほか、[[2001年|2001]]・[[2003年]]（[[平成]]13・15年）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は円形。墳丘は2段築成で、1段目は直径17メートル、2段目は直径10メートル、墳丘裾部からの高さは最大3.7メートルを測る{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。埋葬施設は[[横口式石槨]]で、南方向に開口する。安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石によって構築され、山寄せの立地と合わせて近畿地方の横口式石槨と共通する特徴を示すとして注目される。盗掘に遭っているため副葬品は詳らかでない{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 この谷地久保古墳は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]後半-[[8世紀]]初頭頃の築造と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。南東の野地久保古墳とともに畿内的な横口式石槨を有する特異な古墳であり、被葬者は古代[[白河郡]]における盟主的な立場の人物と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。また、南方に所在する[[下総塚古墳]]（後期の首長墓）と舟田中道遺跡（後期の豪族居館）とともに古墳時代の[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]として認知され、周辺に展開する[[関和久官衙遺跡]]（推定白河郡衙跡）・[[借宿廃寺跡]]からなる古代の白河官衙遺跡群と合わせて、古代白河郡の中心地を示す遺跡群の一角として重要視される古墳である。 古墳域は[[2015年]]（平成17年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「白河舟田・本沼遺跡群」のうち）。 === 来歴 === * [[1926年]]（[[大正]]15年）、測量調査（岩越二郎、[[1936年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1983年]]（[[昭和]]58年）、測量調査（[[網干善教]]、[[1984年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1988年]]（昭和63年）、福島県指定史跡に指定。 * [[2001年|2001]]・[[2003年]]（[[平成]]13・15年）、国の史跡指定に向けた発掘調査：第3・4次調査（白河市教育委員会、[[2002年|2002]]・[[2005年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[2015年]]（平成17年）7月14日、国の[[史跡]]に指定（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|00003447|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}。 == 埋葬施設 == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, sekkaku-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石槨 開口部}}]] 埋葬施設としては[[横口式石槨]]が構築されており、南方向に開口する。石槨の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * 玄室：長さ1.44メートル、幅1.38メートル、高さ1.19メートル * 玄門：長さ0.425メートル、下端幅0.71メートル、高さ0.84メートル * 羨道：長さ0.815メートル、幅0.97メートル、高さ1.17メートル 石槨の石材は安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石。現在は奥壁・側壁・天井石・床石が遺存する。石槨の前庭部は南にハ字形に開き、壁面には川原石を積み、底面には扁平な川原石を敷設する{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 石槨の特徴としては[[中尾山古墳]]（[[奈良県]][[明日香村]]）との共通性が指摘される。中尾山古墳と同様に火葬壺が置かれたとする説の一方、中尾山古墳よりも一回り大きいことから改葬墓とする説もある{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}[[河上邦彦]]『飛鳥発掘物語』扶桑社、2004年、pp. 142-144。。 File:Yachikubo Kofun, 埋葬施設としては[[横口式石槨]]が構築されており、南方向に開口する。石槨の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * 玄室：長さ1.44メートル、幅1.38メートル、高さ1.19メートル * 玄門：長さ0.425メートル、下端幅0.71メートル、高さ0.84メートル * 羨道：長さ0.815メートル、幅0.97メートル、高さ1.17メートル 石槨の石材は安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石。現在は奥壁・側壁・天井石・床石が遺存する。石槨の前庭部は南にハ字形に開き、壁面には川原石を積み、底面には扁平な川原石を敷設する{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|[[野地久保古墳]]方向を望む
（左奥の樹叢）}}]] 福島県南部、[[阿武隈川]]左岸の三方を丘陵に囲まれた丘陵南斜面に築造された古墳である。[[野地久保古墳]]と同じ谷の北西400メートルに位置する。[[1926年]]（[[大正]]15年）・[[1983年]]（[[昭和]]58年）に石室実測調査が実施されているほか、[[2001年|2001]]・[[2003年]]（[[平成]]13・15年）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は円形。墳丘は2段築成で、1段目は直径17メートル、2段目は直径10メートル、墳丘裾部からの高さは最大3.7メートルを測る{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。埋葬施設は[[横口式石槨]]で、南方向に開口する。安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石によって構築され、山寄せの立地と合わせて近畿地方の横口式石槨と共通する特徴を示すとして注目される。盗掘に遭っているため副葬品は詳らかでない{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]後半-[[8世紀]]初頭頃と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。南東の野地久保古墳とともに畿内的な横口式石槨を有する特異な古墳であり、被葬者は古代[[白河郡]]における盟主的な立場の人物と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。また、南方に所在する[[下総塚古墳]]（後期の首長墓）と舟田中道遺跡（後期の豪族居館）とともに古墳時代の[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]として認知され、周辺に展開する[[関和久官衙遺跡]]（推定白河郡衙跡）・[[借宿廃寺跡]]からなる古代の白河官衙遺跡群と合わせて、古代白河郡の中心地を示す遺跡群の一角として重要視される古墳である。 古墳域は[[2015年]]（平成17年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「白河舟田・本沼遺跡群」のうち）。 === 来歴 === * [[1926年]]（[[大正]]15年）、測量調査（岩越二郎、[[1936年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * 墳形は円形。墳丘は2段築成で、1段目は直径17メートル、2段目は直径10メートル、墳丘裾部からの高さは最大3.7メートルを測る{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。埋葬施設は[[横口式石槨]]で、南方向に開口する。安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石によって構築され、山寄せの立地と合わせて近畿地方の横口式石槨と共通する特徴を示すとして注目される。盗掘に遭っているため副葬品は詳らかでない{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]後半-[[8世紀]]初頭頃と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。南東の野地久保古墳とともに畿内的な横口式石槨を有する特異な古墳であり、被葬者は古代[[白河郡]]における盟主的な立場の人物と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。また、南方に所在する[[下総塚古墳]]（後期の首長墓）と舟田中道遺跡（後期の豪族居館）とともに古墳時代の[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]として認知され、周辺に展開する[[関和久官衙遺跡]]（推定白河郡衙跡）・[[借宿廃寺跡]]からなる古代の白河官衙遺跡群と合わせて、古代白河郡の中心地を示す遺跡群の一角として重要視される古墳である。 古墳域は[[2015年]]（平成17年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「白河舟田・本沼遺跡群」のうち）。 === 来歴 === * [[1926年]]（[[大正]]15年）、測量調査（岩越二郎、[[1936年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1983年]]（[[昭和]]58年）、測量調査（[[網干善教]]、[[1984年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1988年]]（昭和63年）、福島県指定史跡に指定。 * [[2001年|2001]]・[[2003年]]（[[平成]]13・15年）、国の史跡指定に向けた発掘調査：第3・4次調査（白河市教育委員会、[[2002年|2002]]・[[2005年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[2015年]]（平成17年）7月14日、国の[[史跡]]に指定（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|00003447|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}。 == 埋葬施設 == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.png|thumb|300px|right|{{center|石槨俯瞰図}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石槨展開図}}]] 埋葬施設としては[[横口式石槨]]が構築されており、南方向に開口する。石槨の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * 玄室：長さ1.44メートル、幅1.38メートル、高さ1.19メートル * 玄門：長さ0.425メートル、下端幅0.71メートル、高さ0.84メートル * 羨道：長さ0.815メートル、幅0.97メートル、高さ1.17メートル 石槨の石材は安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石。現在は奥壁・側壁・天井石・床石が遺存する。石槨の前庭部は南にハ字形に開き、壁面には川原石を積み、底面には扁平な川原石を敷設する{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 石槨の特徴としては[[中尾山古墳]]（[[奈良県]][[明日香村]]）との共通性が指摘される。中尾山古墳と同様に火葬壺が置かれたとする説の一方、中尾山古墳よりも一回り大きいことから改葬墓とする説もある{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}[[河上邦彦]]『飛鳥発掘物語』扶桑社、2004年、pp. 142-144。。 Yachikubo Kofun, sekkaku-3.jpg|内部 古墳|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''谷地久保古墳'''（やちくぼこふん）は、[[福島県]][[白河市]]本沼（もとぬま）にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+白河地域の首長墓{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}} !古墳名 !形状 !埋葬施設 !築造時期 |- |[[下総塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||[[横穴式石室]]||[[6世紀]]後半 |- |舟田中道1号墳||[[円墳]]||横穴式石室||[[7世紀]]前半-7世紀中葉 |- |'''谷地久保古墳'''||円墳||[[横口式石槨]]||7世紀後半-[[8世紀]]初頭 |- |[[野地久保古墳]]||[[上円下方墳]]||横口式石槨||7世紀後半-8世紀初頭 |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|[[野地久保古墳]]方向を望む
（左奥の樹叢）}}]] 福島県南部、[[阿武隈川]]左岸の三方を丘陵に囲まれた丘陵南斜面に築造された古墳である。[[野地久保古墳]]と同じ谷の北西400メートルに位置する。[[1926年]]（[[大正]]15年）・[[1983年]]（[[昭和]]58年）に石室実測調査が実施されているほか、[[2001年|2001]]・[[2003年]]（[[平成]]13・15年）に発掘調査が実施されている。 墳形は円形。墳丘は2段築成で、1段目は直径17メートル、2段目は直径10メートル、墳丘裾部からの高さは最大3.7メートルを測る{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。埋葬施設は[[横口式石槨]]で、南方向に開口する。安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石によって構築され、山寄せの立地と合わせて近畿地方の横口式石槨と共通する特徴を示すとして注目される。盗掘に遭っているため副葬品は詳らかでない{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]後半-[[8世紀]]初頭頃と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。南東の野地久保古墳とともに畿内的な横口式石槨を有する特異な古墳であり、被葬者は古代[[白河郡]]における盟主的な立場の人物と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。また、南方に所在する[[下総塚古墳]]（後期の首長墓）と舟田中道遺跡（後期の豪族居館）とともに古墳時代の[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]として認知され、周辺に展開する[[関和久官衙遺跡]]（推定白河郡衙跡）・[[借宿廃寺跡]]からなる古代の白河官衙遺跡群と合わせて、古代白河郡の中心地を示す遺跡群の一角として重要視される古墳である。 古墳域は[[2015年]]（平成17年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「白河舟田・本沼遺跡群」のうち）。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[1926年]]（[[大正]]15年）、測量調査（岩越二郎、[[1936年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1983年]]（[[昭和]]58年）、測量調査（[[網干善教]]、[[1984年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1988年]]（昭和63年）、福島県指定史跡に指定。 * [[2001年|2001]]・[[2003年]]（[[平成]]13・15年）、国の史跡指定に向けた発掘調査：第3・4次調査（白河市教育委員会、[[2002年|2002]]・[[2005年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[2015年]]（平成17年）7月14日、国の[[史跡]]に指定（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|00003447|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}。 == 埋葬施設 == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|石槨俯瞰図}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石槨展開図}}]] 埋葬施設としては[[横口式石槨]]が構築されており、南方向に開口する。石槨の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * 玄室：長さ1.44メートル、幅1.38メートル、高さ1.19メートル * 玄門：長さ0.425メートル、下端幅0.71メートル、高さ0.84メートル * 羨道：長さ0.815メートル、幅0.97メートル、高さ1.17メートル 石槨の石材は安山岩質溶結凝灰岩（白河石）の切石。現在は奥壁・側壁・天井石・床石が遺存する。石槨の前庭部は南にハ字形に開き、壁面には川原石を積み、底面には扁平な川原石を敷設する{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 石槨の特徴としては[[中尾山古墳]]（[[奈良県]][[明日香村]]）との共通性が指摘される。中尾山古墳と同様に火葬壺が置かれたとする説の一方、中尾山古墳よりも一回り大きいことから改葬墓とする説もある{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}[[河上邦彦]]『飛鳥発掘物語』扶桑社、2004年、pp. 142-144。。 Yachikubo Kofun, sekkaku-3.jpg|内部 {{Japanese Kofun |Name = Yachikubo Kofun |Image = [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, gaikan-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound |Alias = |Affiliation = |Location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Iwaido, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 8|LatitudeSec = 22.80 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 1.75 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} |Size = Diameter 17m
Height 3.7m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} |Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{Location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb Name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Upper round lower square tomb|ja|上円下方墳}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb Name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Height 3.7m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} |Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{Location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb Name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Mound |Alias = |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Iwaido, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 8|LatitudeSec = 22.80 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 1.75 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} |Size = Diameter 17m
Height 3.7m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} |Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Mound |Alias = |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Iwaido, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 8|LatitudeSec = 22.80 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 1.75 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} |Size = Diameter 17m
Height 3.7m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} |Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Height 3.7m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} |Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==

Height 3.7m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} |Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Mound|Alias = |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Iwaido, ]][[Fukushima Prefecture]]|LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 8|LatitudeSec = 22.80|LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 1.75|ISO = JP-07|Shape = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}}|Size = Diameter 17m
Height 3.7m|BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}}|Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs =|ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}|InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb =|HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}|CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}}}}'''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}).== Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;"|+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}!Tomb name!Shape!Burial Structure!Construction Period|-|{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century|-|Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century|-|'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century|-|{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century|}
]][[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]]Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15).The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group.== Archaeological History ==* 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.* 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.* 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture.* 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.* 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}.== Burial Structure ==]][[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]]]][[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]]The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}:* Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters* Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters* Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 metersThe stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144..Yachikubo Kofun, sekkaku-3-2.jpg|InteriorYachikubo Kofun, sekkaku-2-2.jpg|Entrance== References =={{Reflist}}== Sources =={{small|(Sources used for article composition)}}*
