Mound|Alias = |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Iwaido, ]][[Fukushima Prefecture]]|LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 8|LatitudeSec = 22.80|LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 1.75|ISO = JP-07|Shape = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}}|Size = Diameter 17m
Height 3.7m|BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}}|Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs =|ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}|InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb =|HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}|CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}}}}'''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}).== Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;"|+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}!Tomb name!Shape!Burial Structure!Construction Period|-|{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late 6th century|-|Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century|-|'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century|-|{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century|}
]][[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]]Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15).The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group.== Archaeological History ==* 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.* 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.* 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture.* 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.* 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}.== Burial Structure ==]][[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]]]][[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]]The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}:* Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters* Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters* Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 metersThe stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, {{Infobox ancient site|name = Yachikubo Kofun|image = ]][[File:Yachikubo Kofun, gaikan-2.jpg|280px]]
Mound|Alias = |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Iwaido, ]][[Fukushima Prefecture]]|LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 8|LatitudeSec = 22.80|LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 1.75|ISO = JP-07|Shape = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}}|Size = Diameter 17m
Height 3.7m|BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}}|Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs =|ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}|InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb =|HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}|CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}}}}'''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}).== Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;"|+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}!Tomb name!Shape!Burial Structure!Construction Period|-|{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late 6th century|-|Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century|-|'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century|-|{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century|}
]][[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]]Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15).The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group.== Archaeological History ==* 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.* 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.* 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture.* 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.* 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}.== Burial Structure ==]][[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]]]][[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]]The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}:* Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters* Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters* Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 metersThe stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}.Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144..Yachikubo Kofun, sekkaku-3-2.jpg|InteriorYachikubo Kofun, sekkaku-2-2.jpg|Entrance== References =={{Reflist}}== Sources =={{small|(Sources used for article composition)}}* Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Yokoguchi-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoguchi-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Yokoguchi-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Mound |Alias = |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Iwaido, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 8|LatitudeSec = 22.80 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 1.75 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} |Size = Diameter 17m
Height 3.7m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} |Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Mound |Alias = |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Iwaido, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 8|LatitudeSec = 22.80 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 1.75 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} |Size = Diameter 17m
Height 3.7m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} |Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Height 3.7m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} |Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Mound |Alias = |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma Iwaido, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 8|LatitudeSec = 22.80 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 1.75 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳}} |Size = Diameter 17m
Height 3.7m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} |Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Height 3.7m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} |Artifacts = |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |InterredIndividual = |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Yachikubo
Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=8|lat_sec=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site designation; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial Structure == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-shape, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳}}||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}}||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}}, the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient {{ill|Shirakawa District|ja|白河郡}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The chamber's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. Similarities with the {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}} have been noted.
