Height 3.7m |burial = {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} |burial goods = |subsidiary sites = |built = Late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] |InterredIndividual = |Mausoleum = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group]] |CulturalAssets = |Specialnotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|map_dot_label=Yachikubo
Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=8|coordinates=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Shirakawa, Fukushima|Shirakawa, Fukushima]] Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial burial !built |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosozuka Kofun|qq=}}||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Height 3.7m |burial = {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} |burial goods = |subsidiary sites = |built = Late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] |InterredIndividual = |Mausoleum = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group]] |CulturalAssets = |Specialnotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|map_dot_label=Yachikubo
Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=8|coordinates=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Shirakawa, Fukushima|Shirakawa, Fukushima]] Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial burial !built |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosozuka Kofun|qq=}}||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial burial !built |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosozuka Kofun|qq=}}||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=8|coordinates=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Shirakawa, Fukushima|Shirakawa, Fukushima]] Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial burial !built |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosozuka Kofun|qq=}}||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. Height 3.7m |burial = {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} |burial goods = |subsidiary sites = |built = Late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] |InterredIndividual = |Mausoleum = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group]] |CulturalAssets = |Specialnotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|map_dot_label=Yachikubo
Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=8|coordinates=22.80|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=1.75|mark=円墳.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Yachikubo Kofun''' (谷地久保古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Shirakawa, Fukushima|Shirakawa, Fukushima]] Motonuma (本沼), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial burial !built |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosozuka Kofun|qq=}}||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial burial !built |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosozuka Kofun|qq=}}||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial burial !built |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosozuka Kofun|qq=}}||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial burial !built |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosozuka Kofun|qq=}}||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial burial !built |- |{{ill|Shimosozuka Kofun|ja|下総塚古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosozuka Kofun|qq=}}||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||{{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late 6th century |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||Round Kofun||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-7th century |- |'''Yachikubo Kofun'''||Round Kofun||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Corridor-Style Stone Chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144.. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. It is a {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==

[[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, choubou.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View toward {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}} (grove in the left background)}}]] Located in the southern part of Fukushima Prefecture, on the south-facing slope of a hill surrounded by hills on three sides along the left bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]], the kofun is situated 400 meters northwest of {{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}. Detailed surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1926 (Taisho 15) and 1983 (Showa 58), with archaeological excavations carried out in 2001 and 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15). The mound is circular with two tiers: the first tier has a diameter of 17 meters, while the second tier measures 10 meters in diameter. The maximum height from the base is 3.7 meters{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横口式石槨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south. Constructed with cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone), the chamber's design shares characteristics with similar structures in the Kinki region, attracting scholarly interest. Although looted, details of grave goods remain unknown{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The construction period is estimated to be from the late 7th century to the early 8th century, during the {{ill|terminal Kofun period|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/terminal Kofun period|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Along with the nearby Nojikubo Kofun, the mound features distinctive Kinki-style stone chambers, suggesting the interred was a prominent figure in ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. In 2015, the site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group. == Archaeological History == * 1926 (Taisho 15): Measured survey conducted by Jiro Iwakoshi (reported in 1936){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1983 (Showa 58): Measured survey by Yoshinori Abigai (reported in 1984){{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 1988 (Showa 63): Designated a Historic Site of Fukushima Prefecture. * 2001, 2003 (Heisei 13 and 15): Excavations conducted to support National Historic Site Historic Site; reports published in 2002 and 2005 by Shirakawa City Board of Education{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * 2015 (Heisei 27): Designated a National Historic Site as part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group{{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Burial burial == [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Overview}}]] [[File:Yachikubo Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone Chamber Layout}}]] The burial structure consists of a Corridor-Style Stone Chamber opening to the south. The chamber's area are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Main Chamber: Length 1.44 meters, width 1.38 meters, height 1.19 meters * Entrance: Length 0.425 meters, bottom width 0.71 meters, height 0.84 meters * Passageway: Length 0.815 meters, width 0.97 meters, height 1.17 meters The stone chamber's materials are cut andesite welded tuff (Shirakawa stone). Currently, the rear wall, side walls, ceiling, and floor remain intact. The forecourt area widens southward in a V-type, with cobblestones on the walls and flat stones on the floor{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Similarities with the [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]] have been noted. Some scholars suggest it housed cremation urns, while others propose it was a reburial tomb{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}Katsuhiko Kawakami, *Asuka Excavation Stories*, Fusosha, 2004, pp. 142–144..
